questions.title: Character and Its ASCII Code
questions.description:
A char in Java is stored as a 16 bit unsigned number, so every character also has a numeric code. Read one character and print it along with its numeric ASCII code using an int cast.

Input Format:
A single line containing one character.

Output Format:
Char: <character>
ASCII: <numeric code>

Constraints:
The input is one printable ASCII character (code 33 to 126).

questions.title: Integer vs Double Division
questions.description:
Integer division truncates the fraction, while converting an operand to double first keeps it. Read two integers a and b, then print a / b as plain integer division and (double) a / b formatted to exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b separated by a space.

Output Format:
Int division: <a / b>
Double division: <(double) a / b with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
-100000 <= a <= 100000, 1 <= b <= 1000

questions.title: Constants Temperature Log
questions.description:
A weather logger keeps its reference points as final constants so nobody can change them by accident. Read a Celsius temperature, print the freezing and boiling point constants, and whether the reading is below freezing.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: the Celsius temperature.

Output Format:
Celsius: <celsius>
Freezing point: 0
Boiling point: 100
Below freezing: true or false

Constraints:
-50 <= celsius <= 150

questions.title: Smartwatch Lifetime Stats
questions.description:
A smartwatch app estimates lifetime usage stats from the user age. Read the age in years and print the approximate number of days, hours and minutes lived, assuming every year has exactly 365 days.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: age in years.

Output Format:
Years: <age>
Days alive: <age * 365>
Hours alive: <days * 24>
Minutes alive: <hours * 60>

Constraints:
1 <= age <= 100

questions.title: Currency Note Splitter
questions.description:
A bank cashier program splits a withdrawal amount into 500 and 100 rupee notes. Read the amount and print how many notes of each denomination are handed out and what remainder is left (always less than 100).

Input Format:
One line with one integer: the amount.

Output Format:
Amount: <amount>
500 x <amount / 500>
100 x <remainder / 100>
Left: <remainder % 100>

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Memory Footprint Estimator
questions.description:
A systems tool estimates how much memory a huge array of primitives would need before the program allocates it. Read a primitive type name and an item count, then print the total bytes. Sizes are: byte 1, short 2, int 4, long 8, float 4, double 8, char 2, boolean 1. Use long arithmetic so big counts do not overflow the int range.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: type name (one of byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean) and item count (an integer).

Output Format:
Type: <type>
Items: <count>
Bytes: <count * size as a long>

Constraints:
type is one of the eight primitive names, 1 <= count <= 2000000000
questions.inputconstrains: type is one of the eight primitive names, 1 <= count <= 2000000000

questions.title: Cafe Bill Splitter with Casting
questions.description:
A cafe app splits a bill among friends. Read the bill amount in rupees (may include paise as a decimal) and the number of friends. Print the bill, the friend count, the whole rupees each person must pay (truncated with an int cast, never rounded) and the exact per head amount with two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: bill (a decimal number) and friends (an integer).

Output Format:
Bill: <bill with 2 decimals>
Friends: <friends>
Whole rupees each: <(int) per head>
Exact per head: <per head with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= bill <= 100000, 1 <= friends <= 100

questions.title: Cloud Storage Byte Converter
questions.description:
A cloud dashboard converts storage amounts into raw bytes for its billing system. Read a value and a unit (KB, MB or GB), then print the value, the unit and the size in bytes using the 1024 based ladder: 1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB. Use long arithmetic so large values stay exact.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: value (an integer) and unit (KB, MB or GB).

Output Format:
Value: <value>
Unit: <unit>
Bytes: <value converted to bytes as a long>

Constraints:
1 <= value <= 100000000, unit is KB, MB or GB
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= value <= 100000000, unit is KB, MB or GB

questions.title: Safe Addition Auditor
questions.description:
A banking batch job adds two large transaction values stored as long, and adding blindly can overflow the long range. Read two long values, print them, then audit the sum: overflow happens when both values are positive and their sum would exceed the maximum long, or when both are negative and their sum would go below the minimum long. Print the safe sum with status OK, or the overflow report.

Input Format:
One line with two long integers separated by a space.

Output Format:
When safe:
Value A: <a>
Value B: <b>
Safe sum: <a + b>
Status: OK
When overflowing:
Value A: <a>
Value B: <b>
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807

Constraints:
a and b are any two 64 bit long values
questions.sampleoutput2:
Value A: 9000000000000000000
Value B: 9000000000000000000
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807
questions.output1:
Value A: -8000000000000000000
Value B: -8000000000000000000
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807
questions.output3:
Value A: 9223372036854775807
Value B: 1
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807
questions.inputconstrains: a and b are any two 64 bit long values

questions.title: Event Pass with Char Cipher
questions.description:
An event manager prints access passes where each pass carries a secret letter derived with char arithmetic. Read the attendee full name on its own line, then one line with age, tier letter and base price. Tier V gives a 20 percent discount, tier G gives 10 percent, tier P gives none; discounts use integer division. The access code letter is the character A shifted forward by (final price % 26), built with a char cast.

Input Format:
Line 1: full name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: age (an integer), tier (V, G or P), base price (an integer), separated by spaces

Output Format:
Attendee: <name>
Age: <age>
Tier: <tier>
Discount: <base * pct / 100>
Final price: <base - discount>
Access code: <(char) (A + finalPrice % 26)>

Constraints:
1 <= age <= 120, tier is V, G or P, 1 <= price <= 100000
